audit_findings.title: Gross cash add-back may double-count customer-funded operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.606 billion cash add-back, equal to $8.97 per share and 16.8% of the $9.537 billion base equity value; latest filed contract liabilities were $2.2 billion; non-excess cash amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: bridge: cash treated as distributable equity value despite potential operating, customer-funding and Finance liquidity requirements
audit_findings.evidence: At December 28, 2024 and December 30, 2023, contract assets totaled $ 345 million and $ 513 million, respectively, and contract liabilities totaled $ 1.9 billion and $ 1.8 billion, respectively, reflecting timing differences between revenues recognized, billings and payments from customers.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not a demonstrated $1.606 billion double count because contract liabilities do not establish ownership of particular cash dollars. It is nevertheless material: the entire cash addition is large relative to base value, and the record contains no minimum-operating-cash, restricted-cash, customer-funding or captive-Finance liquidity reconciliation proving that it is all excess.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the July 4, 2026 cash by borrowing group against contract liabilities, restricted balances, near-term performance costs, Finance liquidity and minimum operating cash; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The earnings perimeter and separation assumptions may describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: Industrial contributed $145 million of FY2025 segment profit, $99 million of first-half 2026 segment profit and had $2.386 billion of assets at July 4, 2026; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE and growth perimeter plus the equity bridge for separation proceeds, distributed shares, transaction costs and allocated liabilities
audit_findings.evidence: We conduct our business through six operating segments: Textron Aviation, Bell, Textron Systems, Industrial and Textron eAviation, which represent our manufacturing businesses, and Finance, which represents our captive finance business.
audit_findings.explanation: The as-filed perimeter is appropriate while Industrial remains consolidated, but it does not by itself prove that indefinite consolidated projections are consistent with assumptions influenced by the future retained company. Industrial is large enough that omitting its distributed value could understate current holders' entitlement, while retaining its earnings without separation costs or liability allocation could overstate value. No completed-transaction terms or separation bridge establish the net effect.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a separation-date sum-of-the-parts bridge covering Industrial OE, retained-company OE, sale proceeds or distributed shares, stranded and transaction costs, taxes, and allocation of cash, debt, pensions and other liabilities; rerun both combined-holder and retained-company claims.

audit_findings.title: Captive-finance reinvestment may sit outside the owner-earnings deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: 2024 collections exceeded originations by $3 million; 2025 originations exceeded collections by $33 million; first-half 2026 collections exceeded originations by $44 million; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE reinvestment deduction and the receivable capital required to support projected Finance earnings and terminal growth
audit_findings.evidence: The Finance group’s cash flows from investing activities primarily included collections on finance receivables totaling $133 million and $169 million in 2024 and 2023, respectively, partially offset by finance receivable originations of $130 million and $160 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification risk is real, but the record does not demonstrate that the OE calculation omitted receivable funding. Filed net flows are small in the 2024 anchor year and change direction across periods, so they do not establish a normalized capital requirement. A positive terminal growth rate may require additional receivable capital, but that requirement cannot be quantified from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Trace the historical OE schedule against consolidated and borrowing-group cash-flow reclassifications, including originations, collections, credit losses, repossessions and asset sales; estimate normalized receivable capital for each growth scenario and rerun if omitted.

audit_findings.title: Textron has a contingent capital-support obligation to the Finance group
audit_findings.magnitude: No support contributions were required in 2023, 2024 or 2025; July 4, 2026 Finance-group net assets compute to $310 million, $185 million above the $125 million minimum equity requirement; stressed contribution unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: future OE and bridge cash available to common holders could be reduced by mandatory contributions or trapped Finance liquidity
audit_findings.evidence: The agreement, as amended in December 2015, also requires Textron to ensure that TFC maintains fixed charge coverage of no less than 125 % and consolidated shareholders' equity of no less than $ 125 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The support obligation is demonstrated, but no present cash outflow is in the filed results. Current net assets provide balance-sheet headroom over the stated minimum, although the record does not provide enough information to test the 125% fixed-charge-coverage covenant under stress. This is therefore a contingent forward-looking claim rather than a current valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Monitor Finance credit quality and covenant headroom quarterly; stress collateral values, delinquencies, credit losses and fixed-charge coverage, and rerun the bridge if a contribution becomes probable or Finance cash becomes trapped.

audit_findings.title: Pension investment income could inflate OE if the cash-flow adjustment failed
audit_findings.magnitude: $263 million of FY2024 non-service pension and postretirement income, equal to 46.6% of the $564.5 million OE anchor; FY2024 pension cash-flow adjustment was negative $225 million and employer contributions were $44 million; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE anchor and projected OE if pension accounting income was retained instead of corporate cash contributions
audit_findings.evidence: The increase is based on our annual valuation at the end of 2023 and is primarily driven by the impact of actual pension asset returns that exceeded our expected return on plan assets.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential exposure is material, but inclusion is not demonstrated because the filed cash-flow statement contains a substantial pension adjustment that may already remove the noncash income. A line-by-line OE reconciliation is required: retaining the $263 million accounting income would materially inflate the anchor, whereas replacing it with actual normalized corporate contributions would align OE with distributable cash.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile net income, the negative $225 million pension cash-flow adjustment and $44 million of contributions to the $564.5 million anchor; remove non-service pension income, normalize corporate contributions and rerun all scenarios if the adjustment is incomplete.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring charges cannot safely be treated as nonrecurring
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2024 special charges were $78 million, or 13.8% of the $564.5 million OE anchor, comprising $43 million severance, $32 million contract-termination and other costs, and $3 million impairments; FY2023 charges were $126 million, FY2025 net charges were $4 million, and the reserve declined from $71 million to $19 million
audit_findings.mechanism: OE normalization: wholesale add-backs raise the anchor, while failure to normalize genuinely noncash or discontinued costs can lower it
audit_findings.evidence: Special charges of $78 million and $126 million in 2024 and 2023, respectively, include restructuring activities and asset impairment charges as described in Note 15 to the Consolidated Financial Statements on page 62 .
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate repeated charges and material cash-type components, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE calculation added them back. Wholesale exclusion of the $78 million anchor-year charge would be material and could overstate sustainable OE; retaining genuinely noncash impairments or costs tied solely to exited operations could understate it. The plan's substantial completion and lower 2025 charge do not resolve which anchor-year components are recurring adaptation costs.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the OE adjustment schedule and classify each charge by cash payment, recurrence and continuing-business relevance; retain recurring severance and termination costs, normalize genuine noncash or exited-business items, include remaining reserve payments, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.
